answers.rationale: History favors the nearby breakfast hotel when the walk is short and event timing is not early or operationally demanding. A six-minute indoor skybridge walk, sessions after 10:00 a.m., no materials, and only an optional block reception do not justify the block premium. The user’s pattern is contextual rather than a fixed preference for either block or breakfast lodging.

An early 7:15 a.m. plenary inside the Sheraton plus likely rain makes same-building lodging the lower-risk choice. Prior decisions supported paying a modest event-hotel premium when an early in-building session, weather exposure, or morning transfer risk was material, while retaining a refundable lower-cost fallback when possible. This is not a blanket block-hotel rule.

The airport hotel best matches the high-consequence final morning: a 9:00 a.m. airport-business-park debrief followed by a 1:15 p.m. flight. The only downtown obligation is a comparatively late 10:30 a.m. Tuesday meeting, for which one planned rideshare is manageable. History supports locating around the most timing-sensitive final-day anchor when it does not create an early-morning failure point; it does not show a fixed downtown preference.

A hotel-lobby pickup for an 8:00 a.m. campus start is the trip’s critical constraint. Midtown protects that pickup and provides the nearby dinner setup, while the airport hotel would create an early rideshare and traffic/dispatch failure point. The user has repeatedly accepted a higher downtown or meeting-adjacent rate when an early host pickup made the cheaper airport alternative fragile; this remains a context-based policy rather than a stable hotel-area preference.
